# moneypath

> A static analyzer that finds payment logic flaws in Razorpay and Stripe checkouts:
> amounts taken from the client instead of computed server-side, rupee/paise and
> dollar/cent conversion bugs, orders marked paid by browser code, and webhooks that
> never verify their signature. Runs offline with `npx moneypath`, no account or config.

## What problem it solves

Generic security scanners cannot detect payment business-logic flaws. A checkout that
accepts the price from the request body looks structurally identical to one that computes
it server-side. moneypath resolves the difference by tracing the amount argument of a
payment gateway call backwards to its origin.

## Rules

- MP001 (critical) — payment amount originates in the HTTP request and is never recomputed server-side
- MP002 (high) — amount not converted to the gateway minor unit; Razorpay charges paise, Stripe charges cents
- MP003 (high) — minor-unit conversion is unrounded, producing non-integer amounts from float arithmetic
- MP004 (high) — amount multiplied by 100 twice, overcharging 100x
- MP005 (critical) — order marked paid from browser code or an unverified redirect parameter
- MP006 (critical) — payment webhook handler does not verify its signature
- MP007 (high) — amount converted to paise for Cashfree, which bills in rupees as a decimal; the conversion MP002 requires for Razorpay is a 100x overcharge here

## Usage

- CLI: `npx moneypath [path]`
- Report: `npx moneypath --html report.html`
- CI: `npx moneypath --sarif moneypath.sarif --fail-on critical`
- JSON: `npx moneypath --json`
- MCP server: `npx -y moneypath-mcp`, exposing `scan_payment_code` and `list_payment_rules`

Exit codes: 0 clean or below threshold, 1 findings at or above it, 2 bad usage.

## Trust model

Findings are labelled `confirmed` (full path traced) or `review` (pattern matched,
human judgement needed). Values read from the application's own database are treated as
safe even when the client chose which row, because that is the correct pattern. The tool
deliberately prefers false negatives over false positives.

## Scope limits

Syntactic analysis, roughly four hops of backward tracing. Traces across files only for
the common wrapper case: an amount passed into an exported function that calls the
gateway, matched by name plus an import check rather than real module resolution.
Razorpay, Stripe and Cashfree only.
Finds logic flaws, not injection, XSS, or dependency vulnerabilities. A clean run means
these six specific bugs are absent, not that the checkout is secure.
